title: Switch between Telegram and YouTrack
what: The Telegram / YouTrack tabs at the left of the top bar (also on the Settings page) switch between the two modules; the open tab is highlighted, and the other tab shows a red badge for what is new: on Telegram = the tags under Việc cần xử lý › Đang chờ (no AI session yet), on YouTrack = tickets newly given to you since you last opened YouTrack (opening it clears them); with nothing new, the YouTrack tab shows an amber badge = the number of your tickets that need action now. Each sidebar holds only its own module's pages; ⌘K on either side still finds pages of the other.

how.t: Hover "YouTrack" to see new tickets (red badge) or those that need action now (yellow badge), then click to go to YouTrack
Click "Telegram" to go back to the Telegram Inbox

keys: switch module youtrack telegram badge tickets need action now tabs red badge new tickets new messages

title: See your current AI quota
what: The top bar button shows the AI mascot and a ring with the quota used (5-hour session, 7 days) and when it resets; it warns if the AI is not installed or not signed in. By default (Auto) it follows the AI running the everyday work on the open page; pick another AI (Claude, Codex, Agy) right in the button or in Settings › AI › Accounts › "Quota in the top bar".

how.t: Watch the quota ring: it fills up with the % used, turns yellow at 70% used and red from 90%; hover for details, click to open the quota panel
In the panel: pick "Auto" or one AI to always show that AI's quota; click the refresh button to read the quota again

title: Browse the guide to every feature
what: The light bulb in the top bar opens a catalog of every Telegram / YouTrack / Settings feature, no AI needed: type to filter instantly, filter by area, click a feature to see its steps, then "Show me on screen" to have the app light each control to click. Nothing matches: the text you typed goes to the Know-it-all assistant to ask in plain words.

how.t: Click the "User guide" light bulb in the top bar

how: Type in the search box or pick an area: Telegram / YouTrack / Settings
Click a feature to see its steps, then click "Show me on screen"
No matching feature: click "Ask the know-it-all assistant" to ask the AI
keys: guide help user guide light bulb catalog features search tour show me

title: Ask the know-it-all assistant about the app
what: The bot floating in a corner of every page is the user guide and a chat AI assistant in one. Ask in your own words: it searches the guide (and reads the app's own code, read-only, for rules, limits, why a button or item is shown or hidden, citing where), answers with the steps, then adds buttons that take you there: "Open …" opens the right page or Settings group, a feature's name runs a walk-through that lights each control to click. Ask about your own work too ("any messages waiting?", "which tickets are urgent?", "who am I waiting on?"): it reads the Today list, reports how many, the urgent ones first, each with an "Open …" button straight to that message, ticket, Q&A or AI session. Ask follow-ups, it knows which page you are on; the conversation stays as you move between pages. Drag the bot and let go anywhere along a screen edge: it sticks to the nearest edge. It calls you by your YouTrack name (else your Telegram name). Settings › Know-it-all assistant: show / hide the bot, how it shows (Floating, Fixed at the right, In the top bar), its size, position, whether it reads the code, and its own model / effort.

how.t: Click the bot in the screen corner (or F1); drag it to another corner if it covers a button

Type a question (e.g. "why don't I see the Send button?") and press Enter, or click a suggested one; as you type, matching features show right above the box: click one and the app walks you through it, no waiting for the AI

how: Under the answer: click "Open …" to go to the right page, or a feature's name to have the app show you on screen; click "New conversation" to start over

how.t: Change how it shows, its size, position, hide the bot, stop it reading the code or pick its model / effort in Settings › "Know-it-all assistant"

keys: know it all assistant bot user guide help f1 ask ai chat rule condition shown hidden why don't i see button code drag dock corner edge display floating fixed right top bar size

title: AI accounts page (Overview / Model / Usage / History)
what: A panel sliding in from the right with every AI (Claude, Codex, Antigravity), one card each with its own animated mascot: sign-in, quota used, the features using that AI; plus model/effort choice, a cost report and the history of every AI run.

how.t: Click the AI quota button in the top bar, then "Account, usage and history"

how: "Overview" tab: one card per AI with sign in/out, quota used (hover the time to see when it resets) and "Used for" (which features run on that AI, with which model/effort)

how.t: Claude and Codex have free resets from your plan: a ticket icon with the count sits next to "Quota used" (and after "In use" in Settings › AI); click it to see each one (a grant holding several resets shows “×N”), the soonest to expire first (time left; hover for the exact time); click "Reset now" on the one to use and confirm to bring the quota back to 0%. Claude lists its resets only to a recent Claude CLI: run claude update when asked
Open the "Model" tab to choose the model and effort for each feature
Click "Model test" to check the model answers
Open the "Usage" tab for a report of requests, tokens and cost
Pick "30 days" to change the report period (24 hours / 7 days / 30 days)
Open the "History" tab ("Run history") for every AI run by day (the first day of the current page opens by itself), including requests typed in Claude Code / Claude Desktop / Codex

Filter by AI (Claude / Codex / Agy), choose rows per page (50 / 100 / 200 / 500) and page through at the bottom; the download button next to it exports CSV. Paste a session code (YT-… from the YouTrack AI history, REF-… from AI Agent) into the "Find session ID" box to list just that session's runs (every day opens); open a row to see its error and Claude's session (transcript at ~/.claude/projects/*/<session>.jsonl)
